BiblicalUsage: Saul spared the best of the sheep and oxen when he should have destroyed them utterly, and the law says a man who lets his beast eat another's field must pay of the best of his own field. The word is the best part, and both verses show what men do with it.
TheologicalSignificance: I take Saul's best as the warning: he kept the best for himself and called it sacrifice, and Samuel told him obedience is better than sacrifice.
